whatItIs.text: Tiny granules of rolled semolina, steamed rather than boiled in the traditional way; a staple across the Maghreb served under stews.

historyNote.text: The word is likely Berber — the root *KS means 'well rolled, rounded' — and vessels resembling couscoussiers have been found in graves from 3rd-century BC Numidia in Algeria; couscous joined UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2020.

howToChoose.text: Instant (pre-steamed) couscous cooks in minutes and suits weeknights; Moroccan (finer) and pearl (larger) types need proper steaming — check the label before planning dinner.

storage.text: Keep dry in a sealed container in a cool cupboard. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: dry-goods storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Leftover couscous loosens with a fork and a splash of water, then fries into crispy cakes or tosses cold into salads with lemon and herbs.

substitutions.note: gluten-free; smaller germ, cooks by boiling
